correctness.rationale: For each vertex in an occupied part, direct neighbor counting proves the necessary-and-sufficient capacity inequality. Summing occupied-part inequalities proves the half-order bound; one-vertex addition proves upper closure; deletion changes every other occupied-part cross count by exactly one, yielding the two-tight-part minimality criterion. Evaluating capacities at the half-order level proves the parity formula. Dynamic coefficient extraction proves the polynomial formula. A literal-adjacency exhaustive checker independently agrees on all ordered complete-multipartite profiles through order 9.
